pathway.title: COLUMBUS MCKINNON CORP — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is high, and the lower figure the issuer reports depends on annualised earnings. Net debt of USD 2,301.41 million at 2026-09-30, or USD 2,303.44 million pro forma for the common dividend payable on 2026-11-16, is 6.95x issuer-adjusted twelve-month EBITDA of USD 331.19 million, and 6.95x pro forma. The issuer's 4.9x uses USD 467.80 million of earnings that add USD 132.39 million of annualised acquisition earnings and expected synergies, and reported EBITDA of USD 10.03 million is too small to give a ratio. The twelve-month window holds Kito Crosby only from 2026-02-03, so the ratio falls as acquired earnings enter even if net debt does not, and creditors should underwrite a path down from 6.95x rather than the 4.9x already shown. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 14; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation N01

Cash generation does not yet support deleveraging. Free cash flow was USD 4.60 million in H1 FY2027 after a negative USD 15.36 million in Q2 FY2027, which is 2.07% of H1 Adjusted EBITDA, and negative USD 153.19 million over the twelve months to September 2026 after deal and integration payments. Adjusted EBITDA covered interest and debt expense 2.31x in Q2 FY2027, and the issuer plans about USD 150.00 million of repayments in the next twelve months, of which H1 free cash flow covered only 3.07%. The plan therefore rests on a stronger H2, working capital release or revolver and cash use, not on cash flow already earned. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation N02; calculation N03; calculation N04

Liquidity and maturities are the main support. Cash and revolver availability of USD 531.98 million cover the USD 120.88 million of principal scheduled through FY2030 4.40 times, and 95.05% of principal falls after FY2030, with the revolver due in 2031 and the notes and term loan in 2033. The risks inside that comfort are a revolver draw that rose from USD 12.84 million to USD 59.64 million in the September quarter, an AR facility that has no further capacity and needed a lender waiver, and a 2033 wall of USD 1,449.23 million of term loan and USD 900.00 million of notes that refinancing will test. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–30; calculation N05

The business profile is adequate: replacement-driven products and a wide channel give some stability, but concentration and cost exposure limit it. Hoists are 46.68% of net sales, the United States is 58.14%, there is one reporting segment, and most distributors have no written agreement. Raw materials were 51% of cost of products sold, gross margin fell from 33.8% to 30.1% in FY2026 on tariffs, mix and acquisition accounting, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin of 20.6% in Q2 FY2027 against 15.4% is credited by the issuer partly to the acquired business and synergies. Customer concentration is not stated. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 58; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_exhibit99107302026.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation N11; calculation N12

Financial policy is mixed and governance risk is medium. CD&R's USD 800.00 million of preferred equity reduced the debt needed, the preferred is paid in kind in FY2027 guidance, divestiture cash repaid term debt and no shares have been repurchased since FY2025, yet the purchase was largely debt-funded, the preferred claim accretes ahead of common holders, and the agreements that would show consent rights and fees were not supplied. If paid in cash the preferred would take 27.91% to 32.57% of indicative pre-tax free cash flow from guidance. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation N08

Interest-rate and currency exposure are secondary. Floating-rate debt is 62.87% of gross principal, but the issuer states that 100 bp on the term loan adds only about USD 5.00 million of annual cash interest, which is consistent with about USD 965.00 million of swaps, while the market risk text of the annual report contradicts the derivatives note on whether pay-fixed swaps exist. A 10% move in the dollar changes income from operations by about USD 7.26 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 69–70; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 108; calculation N06

cells.text: Designs, makes and markets hoists, crane components, lifting and securement hardware, precision conveyors, digital power and motion control, actuators and rotary unions; five platforms (lifting and securement consumables, installed lifting solutions, precision conveyance, automation, linear motion); one operating and reportable segment
Broad product set under a single reporting segment, so no segment profit is available to test which lines carry the earnings

Hoists 46.68% of net sales (printed as 48%), lifting and securement hardware 13.39%, high-precision conveying systems 12.45%, digital power control and delivery systems 10.28%, actuators and rotary unions 9.06%, industrial cranes 4.98%, technology and specialty solutions and elevator drives 3.17%
One family supplies close to half of sales; the mix is shifting toward consumables as Kito Crosby is added

United States 58.14% of net sales by shipping location, Germany 19.39%, Europe, Middle East and Africa excluding Germany 13.23%, Asia Pacific 4.49%, Latin America 2.67%, Canada 2.08%; Item 1 states 56% for the United States
Diversified, with Japan and Asia Pacific exposure added by Kito Crosby; the two U.S. figures differ by USD 25.48 million

Sold through industrial distributors, rigging shops, independent crane builders, OEMs and government agencies; for the most part no written agreements with distributors; Kito Crosby reports more than 3,500 authorised distributors
Channel loss or a distributor favouring competitors could cut sales; breadth limits dependence on one distributor
Raw materials and components about 51% of cost of products sold in FY2026 and 59% in FY2025; steel, motors, bearings, castings; cost increases passed on through price with a lag
Steel and tariff swings move margin before pricing catches up; the FY2026 ratio mixes perimeters
Net sales USD 539.29 million in Q2 FY2027 of which Kito Crosby USD 300.20 million (55.67%); H1 FY2027 net sales USD 1,070.75 million of which Kito Crosby USD 604.97 million (56.50%)
Earnings now depend on the acquired business
Adjusted EBITDA USD 111.2 million, margin 20.6% against 15.4%; orders USD 562.6 million, book-to-bill 1.0x; Legacy CMCO net sales growth 5.3%
Strong but partly acquisition-driven; legacy growth is modest
USD 519.64 million at 2026-03-31 including USD 199.89 million from Kito Crosby; Legacy CMCO USD 319.75 million against USD 322.52 million a year earlier, when the divested business was still included
The rise in backlog is mainly acquired; the like-for-like legacy change is not established
Capital expenditure USD 17.86 million in FY2026 (1.50% of net sales) and USD 16.46 million in H1 FY2027; USD 45 million to USD 55 million guided for FY2027
Light capital needs support cash conversion once integration costs fade

runs.text: Strength one is liquidity and maturity profile. Cash and revolver availability of USD 531.98 million cover scheduled principal through FY2030 4.40 times, which lowers near-term refinancing and liquidity risk. Strength two is margin and synergy momentum: the Adjusted EBITDA margin rose 520 bp to 20.6% and guidance was raised twice, which would lower leverage if delivered. Strength three is sponsor equity: USD 800.00 million of preferred reduced the debt needed and is paid in kind, preserving cash. Strength four is a replacement-driven franchise whose safety-critical products support repeat demand, with no customer concentration disclosed. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation N05; calculation N12

Weakness one is leverage that depends on annualised earnings: 6.95x on issuer-adjusted EBITDA against the 4.9x the issuer shows, so deleveraging must come from earnings growth and paydown that are not yet in the cash flow. Weakness two is thin free cash flow against fixed interest of USD 185 million to USD 190 million a year, with Q2 FY2027 cover of 2.31x. Weakness three is integration and asset quality: Kito Crosby is 56.50% of H1 sales and goodwill and intangibles are 60.30% of total assets after a USD 200.00 million impairment. Weakness four is cost and demand exposure through steel, tariffs and distributor-led sales. Weakness five is limited visibility of covenant and security terms, with an AR facility waiver and no first lien ratio. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation N01; calculation N02; calculation N14

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On 2026-02-03 Columbus McKinnon closed its all-cash purchase of all of the equity of Kito Crosby Limited from funds associated with KKR. The price was USD 2,700.00 million at announcement, USD 2,811.91 million at closing including USD 184.31 million of acquired cash, and USD 2,821.91 million after a USD 10.00 million final working capital adjustment that was paid after 2026-09-30. Kito Crosby generated about USD 1,100.00 million of revenue in 2024, and its assets and liabilities are carried at preliminary values with USD 931.87 million of goodwill first recorded. A condition of regulatory approval was the sale of the issuer's U.S. power chain hoist and chain operations to Star Hoist, completed on 2026-03-04 for net proceeds of USD 183.98 million. Basis: 10-Q_2025-12-31_cmco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 86–89; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C01

New capital was USD 900.00 million of 7.125% senior secured notes due 2033, issued on 2026-01-30, a USD 1,650.00 million term loan due 2033 and USD 800.00 million of Series A preferred shares sold to CD&R, together USD 3,350.00 million or USD 538.09 million more than the price; a USD 500.00 million revolver replaced the old one and USD 75.00 million of it was drawn at closing. The notes pay interest on 1 February and 1 August, are callable from 2029-02-01 at 103.56% falling to 100.00% from 2031, and carry a change of control offer at 101.0%. The term loan priced at SOFR plus 350 bp with a 50 bp floor and was cut to Term SOFR plus 3.00% on 2026-09-21; it amortises at 0.25% a quarter and sweeps excess cash flow at 50%, 25% or 0% depending on first lien leverage. Guarantors and collateral are not named in the documents read. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 110–113; 10-Q_2025-12-31_cmco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; calculation C02

The AR securitization facility, borrowed through Columbus McKinnon FinCo, LLC with the parent as performance guarantor, allows USD 60.00 million at one-month SOFR plus 110 bp to 2028-08-11 and had USD 42.59 million outstanding at 2026-09-30 with no further capacity. Its lender waived the delinquency and default ratios effective 2026-09-30 and the facility was amended again on 2026-10-29. At 2026-09-30 the revolver had USD 59.64 million drawn, USD 19.28 million of letters of credit and USD 421.08 million available, and total debt was USD 2,412.31 million. The only principal due in FY2027 is USD 17.98 million, and USD 2,320.12 million falls after FY2030. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 114–115; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 162–163; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For creditors, the audited March 2026 statements and the two later quarterly reports give a usable view of the post-acquisition balance sheet and liquidity, yet any trend crossing the February 2026 acquisition of Kito Crosby compares two different perimeters. Covenant tests, guarantor coverage and board rights are known only from the issuer's own summaries, and the revolver maturity is stated two ways in the annual report. These are limits on the evidence, not findings about credit quality.

fields.value: Net debt is 6.95x issuer-adjusted EBITDA for the twelve months to September 2026, above the 4.9x the issuer reports on an annualised basis, so creditors should not rely on the lower figure until Kito Crosby has been owned for a full year. Net debt of USD 2,301.41 million (and USD 2,303.44 million after the dividend payable on 2026-11-16) has not fallen since March 2026, and reported EBITDA of USD 10.03 million over the same twelve months, after a USD 200 million goodwill impairment and deal costs, is too small to give a meaningful ratio.

Issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 331.19 million for the twelve months to September 2026 therefore rests on add-backs the issuer defines: fourteen items added a net USD 249.8 million in fiscal 2026, led by the USD 200 million impairment, with a USD 103.31 million gain on a business sale deducted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation does not yet support the debt. Operating cash flow was negative at USD 125.39 million and free cash flow negative at USD 153.19 million over the twelve months to September 2026, dominated by fiscal 2026 when deal and integration costs were paid; in the first half of fiscal 2027 operating cash flow was USD 21.07 million and free cash flow USD 4.6 million. Capital expenditure is light at 1.57% of net sales, so deleveraging depends on operating cash flow recovering as integration costs fade.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C06; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover is thin and the trailing figure flatters it. Issuer-adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.75x over the twelve months to September 2026, but that period holds only part of a year of interest on the new debt. Interest and debt expense in the September quarter was USD 48.05 million against quarterly issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 111.21 million, a cover of 2.31x, before any benefit from the 50 bp term loan margin cut that began on 2026-09-21.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C06; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for now but fell in the quarter. Cash of USD 110.9 million and revolver availability of USD 421.08 million make USD 531.98 million, down USD 35.17 million since June as revolver borrowings rose from USD 12.84 million to USD 59.64 million. The annual report's schedule shows only USD 17.98 million due in fiscal 2027 and USD 16.5 million in fiscal 2028 before USD 69.9 million in fiscal 2029 and USD 2,320.12 million after fiscal 2030, and the issuer plans to repay about USD 150 million in the next twelve months, already classed as current.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The covenant package gives little comfort that can be measured. The key financial covenant is a first lien leverage ceiling of 7.75x that steps down to 6.25x and is tested only when revolver borrowings exceed 30% of commitments, a trigger that USD 59.64 million drawn against USD 500 million, or 11.93%, does not reach. The first lien ratio itself is not reported, so headroom is not established. The AR securitization lender waived its delinquency and default ratios at 2026-09-30 and the facility was amended again on 2026-10-29, and the documents do not say why.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C19; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside total debt add to the burden. The USD 800 million of 7% convertible preferred shares sold to the sponsor are carried in equity at USD 818.4 million, including payment-in-kind dividends, and would convert into about 43% of the equity; operating lease liabilities were USD 95.72 million and the pension plans were underfunded by USD 78.25 million at March 2026, general and product liability reserves were USD 31.87 million before USD 19.74 million of expected insurance recoveries at September 2026, and USD 20 million is payable to the former owner of Kito Crosby.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is operating momentum and liquidity. The issuer-adjusted EBITDA margin was 20.8% in the first half of fiscal 2027 against 14.7% a year earlier, backlog at March 2026 was USD 519.6 million against USD 322.5 million a year before, and the issuer's annualised measure is 4.9x with cost synergies still to come. Liquidity is also well above scheduled maturities, and the key financial covenant is untested at current revolver use.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C15; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if actual twelve-month issuer-adjusted EBITDA, once Kito Crosby is in for a full year, brings net leverage clearly below the current figure while net debt falls, if free cash flow turns positive after integration costs and cash interest, and if the AR securitization facility passes its tests without waivers. It would worsen if revolver borrowings keep rising toward the 30% trigger, if the waiver is repeated, or if quarterly adjusted EBITDA stops covering interest and debt expense by a wide margin.

fields.value: The Adjusted EBITDA column is the issuer's measure; the leverage and cover charts use reported EBITDA, and fiscal 2026 includes only two months of Kito Crosby.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The bridge reconciles arithmetically but the issuer does not state which items are recurring, cash or realised.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage trajectory and drivers. Debt rose from USD 470.98 million in March 2025 to USD 2,393.01 million in March 2026 because Kito Crosby was bought with a new term loan, USD 900 million of senior secured notes due 2033 and USD 800 million of preferred equity, and then rose a further USD 19.3 million to USD 2,412.31 million by September 2026. Net debt over reported EBITDA is 229.41x in September and not meaningful in March and June because reported EBITDA is negative; the issuer-adjusted ratios of 12.66x, 8.76x and 6.95x fall only as acquired earnings are added to the twelve-month window.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 109; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Coverage. Reported EBITDA does not cover cash interest in any period since March 2026, and issuer-adjusted cover is 3.97x for fiscal 2026 on a full year of the old capital structure and only about two months of the new one, 3.88x to June and 2.75x to September. The quarterly view, 2.31x on interest and debt expense, is the better indicator of the current burden. No funds-from-operations measure is stated by the issuer and none is built here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C06; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash-flow quality. Free cash flow was negative at USD 164.07 million in fiscal 2026, when working capital absorbed cash through the payment of Kito Crosby deal and success fees, and USD 4.6 million in the first half of fiscal 2027. Capital expenditure of 1.57% of net sales leaves little discretionary spending to cut; the split between maintenance and growth is not stated. Cash interest paid is lower than interest and debt expense because the first coupon on the notes was paid only on 2026-08-01.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity adequacy. Cash and revolver availability of USD 531.98 million cover the USD 17.98 million and USD 16.5 million due in the next two fiscal years several times over, and the issuer plans to repay about USD 150 million. The AR securitization facility counts toward liquidity only when the issuer states availability, and at the latest two dates it states no availability; it is secured by U.S. receivables and its lender needed a waiver, so it is treated as working-capital funding rather than committed liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C08; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Data quality and definition risks. The statements reconcile in every column, and the debt instruments reconcile to total debt at March and September. The risks are definitional: reported EBITDA is derived because the issuer states none, the issuer's adjusted measure was redefined in June 2026 and earlier periods were recast, the Credit Agreement measure normalises for a full year of Kito Crosby and expected synergies, and the annual report prints the revolver maturity both as 2028-02-03 and 2031-02-03. Each is recorded in the definition conflict register rather than resolved by assumption.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Subsequent events. The only post-balance-sheet event that changes net debt is the common dividend of USD 2.03 million payable on 2026-11-16, which lifts net debt to USD 2,303.44 million on a mechanical basis. The October 2026 amendment to the AR securitization facility changes its delinquency and default ratios but the documents give no effect on amounts, so no adjustment is made.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interim statements are unaudited and the twelve-month figures are constructed from them. They are on the as-reported perimeter, which holds Kito Crosby only from 2026-02-03 and excludes the divested chain business from 2026-03-04, so growth, margins and leverage across periods are not like for like. The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA here is derived from net income attributable to the Company, income tax, interest and debt expense and depreciation and amortization, and the issuer's adjusted measure is accepted as printed, not tested for recurrence.

fields.value: No covenant headroom, legal ranking or guarantor scope can be established from the documents read, and the AR securitization waiver and amendment documents are not in the set. The annual report's own date is recorded as 2026-06-08 by its signature page while two later quarterly reports say it was filed on 2026-06-02; this changes no figure. This is a financial-data conclusion, not a covenant-capacity or recovery opinion.

fields.value: - High: Issuer-adjusted EBITDA rests on fourteen add-backs for fiscal 2026 that the issuer does not classify as cash or non-cash, recurring or realised, and the Credit Agreement measure adds an annualisation of Kito Crosby, the divestiture and expected synergies that cannot be reproduced. The adjusted ratios are therefore usable as the issuer's view only; component support from the issuer and the credit agreement definitions would close this.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - High: Covenant headroom is not established: the credit agreement's first lien leverage ceiling of 7.75x is not matched by a reported first lien ratio, and the waiver of the AR securitization facility's delinquency and default ratios at 2026-09-30 and its amendment on 2026-10-29 are described but not supplied. The test levels, definitions and any cure terms would be needed to size headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: The acquired business's own statements and pre-acquisition earnings are not supplied, so the twelve-month figures hold Kito Crosby only from 2026-02-03 and no full-year pro forma EBITDA other than the issuer's annualised figure can be built. This understates the earnings base and overstates reported leverage until twelve months of actual results exist.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: Legal ranking, lien priority and guarantor scope across the term loan, notes, revolver and AR facility are not stated in the documents read, so the debt stack chart has no ranked rows and no secured or senior subtotal is formed. The credit agreement, indenture and guarantee schedules would close this.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: The annual report prints the revolver maturity as 2028-02-03 in one paragraph and as 2031-02-03 in the next, and the September 2026 report states 2031-02-03. The later date is used; the earlier one may carry over from the previous facility. The credit agreement would settle it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: The market risk section of the annual report states there are no pay-fixed swaps while the derivatives note describes eleven with a notional of USD 965 million, so the hedged share of the floating-rate debt is not established. Interest sensitivity to rates therefore cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: Free cash flow and operating cash flow include deal, integration and refinancing cash costs that the documents do not separate, so underlying cash generation and the run rate after integration are not established. A cash flow bridge from the issuer would close this.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: The annual report's own date is recorded by its signature page as 2026-06-08 while two later quarterly reports say it was filed on 2026-06-02. This changes no figure but the filing date remains unresolved; the filing record would settle it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: The June 2026 release prints closing cash of 97,234 for fiscal 2026 against 97,023 in the annual report and in its own roll-forward; the annual report figure is used and the difference is 0.211 US$m.

fields.name: Quote

fields.value: - Low: No release states issuer-adjusted EBITDA for fiscal 2024, the third quarter of fiscal 2026 or the nine months to 2025-12-31, so those cells are not supplied; depreciation and amortization for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 is calculated because no document prints it.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: The company reports one segment, so no segment revenue schedule is built, and capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth; backlog and receivable statistics after March 2026 are not stated in the later releases, and the issuer states no funds-from-operations measure, so none is built.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Small uncommitted non-U.S. bank lines of USD 5.438 million, of which USD 0.566 million was drawn, and USD 18.757 million of bank guarantees in use are not part of the debt instrument table or total debt, and where the drawn amount is classified is not stated; the amounts are immaterial to leverage but would be debt-like if drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Pension and operating lease balances are taken at March 2026 only and their September 2026 values are not extracted, and the terms of the preferred dividend between cash and payment in kind are stated but the election for the current year is not.

fields.value: Business, transaction, ownership and governance fact pack for COLUMBUS MCKINNON CORP (issuer id cmco), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway. The scope is the Kito Crosby acquisition and its financing, the CD&R preferred equity, the operating model and the governance and sponsor-behaviour evidence in the seven supplied filings and releases.

fields.value: Creditors now rest on a larger and more leveraged industrial business whose credit case depends on integrating Kito Crosby, a USD 2,811.91 million all-cash purchase financed by new capital that was 76.12% secured debt and 23.88% CD&R senior preferred.

fields.value: The business sells products that management calls safety-critical through distributors, and Kito Crosby already supplies 56.50% of first-half sales, but the issuer's own leverage measure still adds back USD 132.39 million of annualised earnings and synergies. Sponsor and governance risk is medium: CD&R supplied equity and shows no documented extraction, yet the investment agreement, board terms and proxy statement were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A material part of the earnings behind the leverage measure is annualised, not yet earned. Kito Crosby supplied 15.76% of FY2026 net sales but 56.50% of H1 FY2027 net sales, and the issuer's Credit Agreement measure adds USD 132.39 million, or 28.30% of its USD 467.80 million twelve-month earnings figure, for a full year of Kito Crosby, the divestiture and expected synergies. That add-back was 59.94% of the measure at March 2026, when it included USD 70.64 million of expected synergies. Creditors should read the 4.9x ratio as management-normalised, not measured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The capital structure is debt-heavy with a growing senior equity layer rather than common equity beneath the debt. New secured debt of USD 2,550.00 million and USD 800.00 million of 7% preferred raised USD 538.09 million more than the purchase price, a sum the filings do not break down between refinancing, fees and cash. The preferred accreted USD 37.43 million through September 2026 and the issuer guides to paying it in kind during FY2027; paid in cash it would cost about USD 58.62 million a year on a simple calculation, against USD 4.04 million of common dividends in H1 FY2027. Debt holders gain from the cash retained, but the preferred claim grows ahead of common holders and would compete for cash if the election changed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CD&R holds influence and a senior claim, but the documents read show no extraction, so governance risk is medium rather than high or low. The investor owns all of the Series A preferred, may name up to three directors, has preemptive rights to keep its pro rata stake and would hold about 43.45% as converted at September 2026 on a calculation that ignores unvested awards, up from 42.48% at issue because the dividend accretes. The annual report itself warns that the investor's interests may differ from other holders. No fees, related-party dealings or creditor-adverse transactions appear in the filings read, but the agreements that would show consent rights and fees were not supplied, so capacity and willingness cannot be separated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating franchise is defensive in its consumables and installed base, yet sales are cyclical, distributor-led and exposed to steel and component costs. Management describes the safety-critical products as frequently replaced, most distributors have no written agreement with the issuer, and raw materials were 51% of cost of products sold in FY2026 against 59% a year earlier, a fall that overstates any improvement because the numerator excludes Kito Crosby while the denominator includes it. Hoists are 46.68% of sales, the precision conveying line shrank 3.94% and carries a USD 200.00 million goodwill impairment, and legacy growth is modest: Legacy CMCO net sales grew 5.3% in Q2 FY2027, while total backlog rose 61.12% by March 2026 mainly because Kito Crosby brought USD 199.89 million of it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation since closing has favoured deleveraging over distributions, which is supportive but not yet proof. The term loan was cut by USD 191.08 million on the divestiture, USD 7.10 million more than its USD 183.98 million of net proceeds. The issuer plans about USD 150.00 million of repayments in the next twelve months, no shares have been repurchased since FY2025 and the common dividend stayed at USD 0.07 per quarter. Against that, integration and deal costs were USD 65.65 million in FY2026 and USD 30.26 million in H1 FY2027, free cash flow was USD 4.60 million in H1 FY2027 after a negative USD 15.36 million in Q2 FY2027, and capital expenditure is guided up to USD 45 million to USD 55 million. Only USD 14.53 million of the planned paydown is scheduled amortisation, so the rest is an intention, not a maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure supports monitoring, but several items are inconsistent, undated or unexplained, and each caps confidence. The purchase price is printed as USD 2,700.00 million, USD 2,811.91 million and USD 2,821.91 million at announcement, closing and after a final adjustment paid after quarter end. The revolver maturity is printed as 2028 and 2031, and the repayment table supports 2031. The AR facility lender waived its delinquency and default tests at 2026-09-30 and the facility was amended on 2026-10-29 with no reason given. The separation agreement with the officer who signed the annual report as chief financial officer and the successor's offer letter are dated 2026-07-01, which dates a change that the Source readiness analysis could not date, and no reason is stated. Kito Crosby was excluded from the FY2026 internal control assessment while holding 69.72% of consolidated total assets. These are monitoring points, not evidence of conduct.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is trading momentum and cash retention. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 20.6% in Q2 FY2027 against 15.4% a year earlier, orders rose 122% largely through the acquisition, and the issuer raised its FY2027 net sales and Adjusted EBITDA guidance twice, to USD 2,130 million to USD 2,170 million and USD 425 million to USD 440 million. Liquidity of USD 531.98 million is far above the USD 17.98 million of principal due in FY2027 and the USD 69.90 million due in FY2029, the sponsor's USD 800.00 million is equity behind the debt and is being paid in kind, and the 50 bp margin cut lowers interest cost. If these hold, the medium governance rating and the doubts about the annualised leverage measure would both ease.

fields.value: The view would improve if the investment agreement and proxy statement show only customary investor consent rights and no fees, if FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA lands within guidance with synergies realised in cash, and if the planned USD 150.00 million paydown is made while preferred dividends stay in kind. It would worsen if the issuer elects cash preferred dividends, funds further sponsor-linked acquisitions with debt, repeats the AR facility waiver, or lets revolver borrowings reach the 30% level at which the first lien leverage covenant is tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-02-03 Columbus McKinnon closed its all-cash purchase of all of the equity of Kito Crosby Limited from funds associated with KKR. The price was USD 2,700.00 million at announcement, USD 2,811.91 million at closing including USD 184.31 million of acquired cash, and USD 2,821.91 million after a USD 10.00 million final working capital adjustment that was paid after 2026-09-30. Kito Crosby generated about USD 1,100.00 million of revenue in 2024, and its assets and liabilities are carried at preliminary values with USD 931.87 million of goodwill first recorded. A condition of regulatory approval was the sale of the issuer's U.S. power chain hoist and chain operations to Star Hoist, completed on 2026-03-04 for net proceeds of USD 183.98 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New capital was USD 900.00 million of 7.125% senior secured notes due 2033, issued on 2026-01-30, a USD 1,650.00 million term loan due 2033 and USD 800.00 million of Series A preferred shares sold to CD&R, together USD 3,350.00 million or USD 538.09 million more than the price; a USD 500.00 million revolver replaced the old one and USD 75.00 million of it was drawn at closing. The notes pay interest on 1 February and 1 August, are callable from 2029-02-01 at 103.56% falling to 100.00% from 2031, and carry a change of control offer at 101.0%. The term loan priced at SOFR plus 350 bp with a 50 bp floor and was cut to Term SOFR plus 3.00% on 2026-09-21; it amortises at 0.25% a quarter and sweeps excess cash flow at 50%, 25% or 0% depending on first lien leverage. Guarantors and collateral are not named in the documents read.

fields.value: The AR securitization facility, borrowed through Columbus McKinnon FinCo, LLC with the parent as performance guarantor, allows USD 60.00 million at one-month SOFR plus 110 bp to 2028-08-11 and had USD 42.59 million outstanding at 2026-09-30 with no further capacity. Its lender waived the delinquency and default ratios effective 2026-09-30 and the facility was amended again on 2026-10-29. At 2026-09-30 the revolver had USD 59.64 million drawn, USD 19.28 million of letters of credit and USD 421.08 million available, and total debt was USD 2,412.31 million. The only principal due in FY2027 is USD 17.98 million, and USD 2,320.12 million falls after FY2030.

fields.value: Columbus McKinnon has an adequate business and a stretched financial profile, so creditors depend on Kito Crosby earnings and synergies arriving while liquidity and long maturities buy time.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity of USD 531.98 million and no scheduled principal above USD 69.90 million before 2031 support the credit, but quarterly interest cover is 2.31x, free cash flow was only USD 4.60 million in H1 FY2027 and the issuer's 4.9x leverage figure rests on annualised earnings. The main downside is a margin reversal in a distributor-led, steel-exposed business that carries fixed interest charges of USD 185 million to USD 190 million a year.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation N02; calculation N05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is high, and the lower figure the issuer reports depends on annualised earnings. Net debt of USD 2,301.41 million at 2026-09-30, or USD 2,303.44 million pro forma for the common dividend payable on 2026-11-16, is 6.95x issuer-adjusted twelve-month EBITDA of USD 331.19 million, and 6.95x pro forma. The issuer's 4.9x uses USD 467.80 million of earnings that add USD 132.39 million of annualised acquisition earnings and expected synergies, and reported EBITDA of USD 10.03 million is too small to give a ratio. The twelve-month window holds Kito Crosby only from 2026-02-03, so the ratio falls as acquired earnings enter even if net debt does not, and creditors should underwrite a path down from 6.95x rather than the 4.9x already shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 14; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation N01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation does not yet support deleveraging. Free cash flow was USD 4.60 million in H1 FY2027 after a negative USD 15.36 million in Q2 FY2027, which is 2.07% of H1 Adjusted EBITDA, and negative USD 153.19 million over the twelve months to September 2026 after deal and integration payments. Adjusted EBITDA covered interest and debt expense 2.31x in Q2 FY2027, and the issuer plans about USD 150.00 million of repayments in the next twelve months, of which H1 free cash flow covered only 3.07%. The plan therefore rests on a stronger H2, working capital release or revolver and cash use, not on cash flow already earned.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturities are the main support. Cash and revolver availability of USD 531.98 million cover the USD 120.88 million of principal scheduled through FY2030 4.40 times, and 95.05% of principal falls after FY2030, with the revolver due in 2031 and the notes and term loan in 2033. The risks inside that comfort are a revolver draw that rose from USD 12.84 million to USD 59.64 million in the September quarter, an AR facility that has no further capacity and needed a lender waiver, and a 2033 wall of USD 1,449.23 million of term loan and USD 900.00 million of notes that refinancing will test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–30; calculation N05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is adequate: replacement-driven products and a wide channel give some stability, but concentration and cost exposure limit it. Hoists are 46.68% of net sales, the United States is 58.14%, there is one reporting segment, and most distributors have no written agreement. Raw materials were 51% of cost of products sold, gross margin fell from 33.8% to 30.1% in FY2026 on tariffs, mix and acquisition accounting, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin of 20.6% in Q2 FY2027 against 15.4% is credited by the issuer partly to the acquired business and synergies. Customer concentration is not stated.

fields.value: Financial policy is mixed and governance risk is medium. CD&R's USD 800.00 million of preferred equity reduced the debt needed, the preferred is paid in kind in FY2027 guidance, divestiture cash repaid term debt and no shares have been repurchased since FY2025, yet the purchase was largely debt-funded, the preferred claim accretes ahead of common holders, and the agreements that would show consent rights and fees were not supplied. If paid in cash the preferred would take 27.91% to 32.57% of indicative pre-tax free cash flow from guidance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest-rate and currency exposure are secondary. Floating-rate debt is 62.87% of gross principal, but the issuer states that 100 bp on the term loan adds only about USD 5.00 million of annual cash interest, which is consistent with about USD 965.00 million of swaps, while the market risk text of the annual report contradicts the derivatives note on whether pay-fixed swaps exist. A 10% move in the dollar changes income from operations by about USD 7.26 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is earnings momentum and delivery against guidance. Adjusted EBITDA margin rose 520 bp to 20.6% in Q2 FY2027, Legacy CMCO net sales grew 5.3%, synergies are described as ahead of plan, and guidance for Adjusted EBITDA was raised twice, to USD 425 million to USD 440 million. That guidance needs H2 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 202.35 million to USD 217.35 million against USD 222.65 million in H1 FY2027, so it does not require improvement, and the 50 bp term loan margin cut saves about USD 7.25 million a year. If H2 delivers and net debt starts to fall, leverage on the issuer's own basis would approach the reported 4.9x with real earnings behind it.

fields.value: The view would improve if quarterly free cash flow turns clearly positive after integration costs, if the planned paydown is made from cash flow, if the AR facility passes its tests without waivers, and if the missing agreements show customary investor rights. It would worsen if book-to-bill falls below 1.0x, if the Adjusted EBITDA margin slips back toward the 15.2% of FY2026, if revolver borrowings approach the 30% covenant trigger, or if the preferred dividend is paid in cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Columbus McKinnon designs, makes and markets lifting, rigging, conveying and motion-control products and, since 2026-02-03, includes Kito Crosby, a lifting and securement business that supplied 56.50% of H1 FY2027 net sales. The issuer describes its consumables as safety-critical and frequently replaced, which is management language but points to repeat demand tied to inspection cycles, while hoists, cranes and conveyors depend on industrial capital spending. Sales go mainly through distributors and crane builders, 44% of FY2026 sales were outside the United States, and there is one reporting segment. For creditors the replacement element supports cash-flow visibility and debt service, the cyclical element limits it, and the larger scale after the acquisition helps access to capital markets without removing the integration risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CD&R XII Keystone Holdings, L.P. holds all of the Series A preferred, about 43% of the equity as converted, may name up to three directors and has preemptive rights, while the common shares are listed and the common holders are not named in the documents supplied. The parent borrows under the 2026 credit agreement and issued the notes, unnamed subsidiaries guarantee the notes, and the AR facility is borrowed through a financing subsidiary with the parent as performance guarantor. Structural priority, guarantor coverage and any unrestricted group cannot be established without the indenture and credit agreement, and the sponsor's willingness to support or extract cannot be inferred from its identity. Sponsor and governance risk is medium on documented behaviour: equity was supplied and no extraction is recorded, but the consent rights, fees and board composition are not visible.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is partly recurring and partly cyclical. In FY2026 price added USD 21.54 million and volume USD 10.15 million to net sales, and in Q2 FY2027 price added USD 10.06 million against USD 2.34 million from volume, so price supplied 81.14% of the organic gain in the quarter. That points to pricing power, but it also means volume growth is thin, and the issuer ties demand to industrial capacity utilisation, production indices, tariffs and interest rates. Backlog rose 61.12% to USD 519.64 million by March 2026 mainly through Kito Crosby, long-term backlog was 50.8% of the total, and book-to-bill was 1.0x in Q2 FY2027. Sales rest on distributors that choose what to stock and have no written agreements, and no customer or distributor concentration is stated. Revenue is therefore likely more predictable in its consumable and installed-base share, on management's description, and cyclical and discretionary in its project share, and not shown to be concentrated or structurally declining apart from the 3.94% fall in precision conveying.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are weighted to materials and the pass-through is lagged. Raw materials and components were 51% of cost of products sold in FY2026, bought from a limited set of preferred suppliers on company-wide terms, and the issuer reports higher steel and component costs and tariffs. In FY2026 material inflation, tariffs and other cost changes net of price took USD 5.88 million from gross profit, unfavourable mix took USD 7.91 million and the divested business took USD 6.69 million, and the gross margin fell to 30.1% from 33.8% with USD 36.80 million of inventory step-up in cost of sales. In Q2 FY2027 the gross margin was 34.8% against 34.5% and the Adjusted gross margin 36.5% against 35.3%. The split between fixed and variable cost is not stated, so operating leverage cannot be measured; the evidence supports defending margins against input costs with price, with synergy savings as extra cushion, and does not show how margins behave under a volume fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 57–58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation N12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital needs are light and conversion of EBITDA to cash is weak for now. Capital expenditure was 1.50% of FY2026 net sales and USD 16.46 million in H1 FY2027, with USD 45 million to USD 55 million guided for FY2027, so capex is a lever of some size. Free cash flow was 2.07% of H1 FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA because interest, integration costs of USD 24.30 million year to date, cash taxes and an USD 55.04 million working capital outflow absorbed it, and net cash paid for income taxes was USD 45.85 million in FY2026 despite a net loss. Operating lease payments of USD 23.84 million fall due in FY2027. Deal-related payments depressed FY2026 and the first half, so conversion should improve as they end, but the guidance arithmetic leaves only USD 180.00 million to USD 210.00 million before taxes, integration and working capital, which is the amount that would fund the planned paydown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 149; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 55–56; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation N03; calculation N08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is the force that matters most for margins: the industry is fragmented, rivals include larger groups and some have greater financial resources and less debt, and competition on price could cut margin. Buyer power sits with distributors that decide what to stock and have no written agreements with the issuer, which limits pricing if they favour a rival. Supplier power is moderate: materials are available from several sources but the issuer buys from a limited set of preferred suppliers, and supply constraints have raised cost and lead times. The threat of new entrants and of substitutes is not established in the documents supplied, so no credit conclusion is drawn on either.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two categories change credit capacity. Political and regulatory factors: tariffs raised input costs, and regulatory approval of the acquisition required the sale of the U.S. power chain hoist and chain business, which contributed USD 123.05 million of FY2026 sales and none after 2026-03-04. Economic factors: demand follows industrial capacity utilisation and production, 62.87% of debt floats, and 44% of sales are outside the United States, where a 10% move in the dollar changes income from operations by about USD 7.26 million. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 69; EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation N06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are the replacement-driven consumable base, a broad distributor and service network, liquidity of USD 531.98 million with no large maturity before 2031, and sponsor equity of USD 800.00 million. Weaknesses are leverage that is high on actual earnings, thin free cash flow, goodwill and intangibles of 60.30% of total assets, concentration in hoists and in the United States, and cost exposure to steel and tariffs. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are synergy delivery and margin expansion, the 50 bp margin cut, and paydown from a recovering free cash flow. Threats that could weaken it are an industrial downturn with distributor destocking, a cash election on the preferred, a second waiver on the AR facility, and refinancing the USD 2,349.23 million of term loan and notes due in 2033 at higher leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 110–111; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation N05; calculation N14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength one is liquidity and maturity profile. Cash and revolver availability of USD 531.98 million cover scheduled principal through FY2030 4.40 times, which lowers near-term refinancing and liquidity risk. Strength two is margin and synergy momentum: the Adjusted EBITDA margin rose 520 bp to 20.6% and guidance was raised twice, which would lower leverage if delivered. Strength three is sponsor equity: USD 800.00 million of preferred reduced the debt needed and is paid in kind, preserving cash. Strength four is a replacement-driven franchise whose safety-critical products support repeat demand, with no customer concentration disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation N05; calculation N12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness one is leverage that depends on annualised earnings: 6.95x on issuer-adjusted EBITDA against the 4.9x the issuer shows, so deleveraging must come from earnings growth and paydown that are not yet in the cash flow. Weakness two is thin free cash flow against fixed interest of USD 185 million to USD 190 million a year, with Q2 FY2027 cover of 2.31x. Weakness three is integration and asset quality: Kito Crosby is 56.50% of H1 sales and goodwill and intangibles are 60.30% of total assets after a USD 200.00 million impairment. Weakness four is cost and demand exposure through steel, tariffs and distributor-led sales. Weakness five is limited visibility of covenant and security terms, with an AR facility waiver and no first lien ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business dimensions. Scale and market position is average: pro forma FY2026 net sales of USD 2,035.00 million with leading positions that are management claims and no market share figures. Competitive advantage is average: brands, safety-critical function and a service network support it, but retention, switching cost and pricing power beyond price increases of USD 21.54 million in FY2026 are not evidenced. Business diversification is average: eight product lines and six regions, offset by hoists at 46.68%, the United States at 58.14%, one segment and undisclosed customer concentration.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 150; calculation N11; calculation N13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating and cash dimensions. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capex is 1.50% of sales and can be cut, but the fixed cost share is not stated. Margin stability is average: the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.3% in FY2025, 15.2% in FY2026 and 20.8% in H1 FY2027 with tariffs and mix hurting FY2026 and the acquired business and synergies helping since. Free cash flow stability is weak: free cash flow was negative USD 153.19 million over the twelve months to September 2026 and USD 4.60 million in H1 FY2027, and conversion was 2.07% of Adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 61; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation N03; calculation N12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial dimensions. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: the issuer placed USD 900.00 million of notes and a USD 1,650.00 million term loan in early 2026 and cut the term loan margin by 50 bp in September, but no rating or market price is supplied and leverage is high. Liquidity position is average: USD 531.98 million and a distant maturity profile, against revolver draws that rose and an AR facility without capacity. Financial policy and governance is average with low confidence: equity support, in-kind preferred dividends and divestiture paydown against leveraged acquisition funding and missing agreements. Main supports are liquidity, maturities and margin momentum; constraints are leverage, cash conversion and integration; the trend is improving in margin and worsening in revolver use; missing data are the covenant ratio, rating, Kito Crosby standalone earnings and the investor agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–29; calculation N05; calculation N09; calculation N14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the issuer guides to FY2027 net sales of USD 2,130 million to USD 2,170 million, Adjusted EBITDA of USD 425 million to USD 440 million and interest expense of USD 185 million to USD 190 million. The guidance is 5.65% above pro forma FY2026 sales at its midpoint and needs H2 Adjusted EBITDA no higher than H1, which supports it, while guided Adjusted EBITDA covers guided interest 2.24x to 2.38x, so deleveraging depends on cash conversion and the planned paydown, not on cover. Company tailwinds are synergy delivery, the margin cut and lower deal costs; company headwinds are interest cost, integration spend and a cash election on the preferred. Sector tailwinds named by the issuer are automation and labour productivity trends and growth in Asia and other emerging markets; sector headwinds are tariffs, steel and component costs and a slowdown in industrial production. Over three to five years the 2029 call date of the notes, the 2031 revolver and the 2033 term loan and notes make deleveraging before 2033 the central task.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 55–57; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 110–111; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation N02; calculation N07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is an industrial slowdown with steel and tariff cost pressure that leads distributors, who hold the stocking decision and have no written agreements, to cut orders. The first operational break is a fall in short-cycle orders, with book-to-bill below 1.0x, followed by price giving way to volume and gross margin falling back from the 34.1% Adjusted gross margin of FY2026. Financially, on illustrative arithmetic that returns the Adjusted EBITDA margin to the 15.20% of FY2026 on the guided sales midpoint of USD 2,150 million, Adjusted EBITDA would be USD 326.80 million, interest cover 1.74x, and EBITDA less guided interest and capex USD 89.30 million before taxes, integration and working capital. Cash taxes at the FY2026 level of USD 45.85 million would leave USD 43.45 million, so the planned USD 150.00 million paydown would not be met from cash flow and the revolver would fund the gap. Revolver borrowings could rise by USD 90.36 million, or USD 71.08 million if letters of credit count, before the 30% level at which the first lien leverage covenant is tested, and the ratio against its 7.75x ceiling is not reported. Management levers are capex, which can be cut, the in-kind preferred dividend, a common dividend of USD 8.04 million a year, working capital release from USD 567.55 million of inventory and synergy savings. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis within 12 to 24 months because no principal above USD 69.90 million falls due before 2031, but it is not sufficient to protect the deleveraging plan, and the observable triggers are book-to-bill, the Adjusted EBITDA margin, revolver use, and any new AR facility waiver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation N09; calculation N10; calculation N12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Columbus McKinnon presents an adequate business profile supported by replacement-driven products, a wide channel and added scale, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 6.95x on issuer-adjusted EBITDA (6.95x pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-11-16), thin free cash flow and integration risk. Cash-flow durability appears weak today and not yet demonstrated, because free cash flow was 2.07% of H1 Adjusted EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on cutting leverage before the 2033 term loan and notes come due, on extending the AR facility due 2028-08-11 and on keeping the revolver unused near the 30% covenant level. The primary downside path is a margin reversal on fixed interest charges that forces revolver use and defers deleveraging. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and first lien ratio, the investor agreements, Kito Crosby's standalone earnings, a rating and market prices. Top risk: leverage that depends on annualised earnings and unproven free cash flow.
